exercises.name: Dumbbell Squat
exercises.content:
**How to do Dumbbell Squats:**

1. **Starting Position:** Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, hold dumbbells at your sides or at shoulder height
2. **Movement:** Push hips back, bend knees to lower down, keep chest up and core tight
3. **Depth:** Go down until thighs are parallel to ground (or as comfortable)
4. **Return:** Drive through heels to stand back up, squeeze glutes at top

**Common Mistakes:**
- Knees caving inward - keep them aligned with toes
- Leaning too far forward - keep chest up
- Rising on toes - keep weight in heels

**Knee-Safe Modifications:**
- Box squats: Sit back to a box to control depth
- Goblet squats: Hold dumbbell at chest, easier on knees
- Limit depth: Don't go below parallel if knee hurts
- Wider stance: Reduces knee stress

exercises.name: Push-ups
exercises.content:
**How to do Push-ups:**

1. **Starting Position:** Plank position, hands slightly wider than shoulders, body straight from head to heels
2. **Descent:** Bend elbows to lower chest toward ground, elbows at 45-degree angle
3. **Bottom:** Lower until chest nearly touches ground
4. **Push Up:** Press through hands to return to start

**Progressions:**
- **Easier:** Wall push-ups → Incline push-ups → Knee push-ups → Full push-ups
- **Harder:** Decline push-ups → Diamond push-ups → One-arm push-ups

**Common Mistakes:**
- Sagging hips - keep core tight
- Flaring elbows out - keep at 45 degrees
- Not going deep enough - chest should nearly touch floor

exercises.name: Dumbbell Row
exercises.content:
**How to do Dumbbell Rows:**

1. **Starting Position:** Hinge forward at hips, support with one hand on bench, dumbbell in other hand hanging down
2. **Pull:** Drive elbow back and up, pulling dumbbell toward hip
3. **Squeeze:** Squeeze shoulder blade at top
4. **Lower:** Control descent back to start

**Tips:**
- Pull with elbow, not hand
- Keep back flat, don't rotate torso
- Full range of motion - stretch at bottom, squeeze at top

**Variations:**
- Bent-over row: Both arms at once
- Chest-supported row: Less lower back stress

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
exercises.content:
**How to do Dumbbell Shoulder Press:**

1. **Starting Position:** Sit or stand, dumbbells at shoulder height, palms forward
2. **Press:** Push dumbbells straight overhead until arms fully extended
3. **Top:** Dumbbells should be close together overhead
4. **Lower:** Control descent back to shoulders

**Common Mistakes:**
- Arching lower back - keep core tight
- Pressing forward instead of up - straight overhead
- Locking elbows hard - soft lockout at top

**Shoulder-Safe Tips:**
- Don't go too heavy - control is key
- Full range of motion
- Neutral grip (palms facing) is easier on shoulders

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.content:
**How to do Planks:**

1. **Starting Position:** Forearms on ground, elbows under shoulders, body straight from head to heels
2. **Hold:** Maintain position, squeeze core and glutes
3. **Breathing:** Breathe normally, don't hold breath

**Key Points:**
- Body in straight line - don't let hips sag or pike up
- Squeeze glutes and core tight
- Look at floor to keep neck neutral

**Progressions:**
- Start with 20-30 seconds
- Build to 60 seconds
- Add variations: side planks, plank shoulder taps

**Common Mistakes:**
- Sagging hips - hardest mistake to avoid
- Holding breath - breathe normally
- Hiking hips too high - straight line

exercises.name: Lunges
exercises.content:
**How to do Lunges:**

1. **Starting Position:** Stand tall, feet hip-width apart
2. **Step Forward:** Take big step forward with one leg
3. **Lower:** Drop back knee toward ground, front thigh parallel
4. **Rise:** Push through front heel to return to start

**Knee-Safe Modifications:**
- Shorter step: Reduces knee stress
- Reverse lunges: Step back instead of forward (easier on knees)
- Split squats: Keep feet in lunge position, just go up and down

**Common Mistakes:**
- Front knee past toes - step further forward
- Leaning forward - keep torso upright
- Back knee slamming down - control the descent

exercises.name: Deadlifts
exercises.content:
**How to do Deadlifts:**

1. **Setup:** Barbell over mid-foot, feet hip-width, shins close to bar
2. **Grip:** Reach down, grip bar just outside legs
3. **Position:** Chest up, back flat, hips between knees and shoulders
4. **Pull:** Drive through heels, extend hips and knees together
5. **Lockout:** Stand tall, squeeze glutes
6. **Lower:** Push hips back, bend knees once bar passes them

**Safety Tips:**
- Keep back flat - never round lower back
- Bar stays close to body throughout
- Drive with legs, not just pulling with back
- Use lighter weight until form is perfect

**Common Mistakes:**
- Rounding back - most dangerous
- Bar drifting away from body
- Not fully locking out at top

injury_guides.content:
**Training with Knee Issues:**

**Exercises to Avoid:**
- Deep squats below parallel
- Lunges (especially forward lunges)
- Leg extensions (high shear force on knee)
- Box jumps or plyometrics

**Safe Alternatives:**
- Box squats (controlled depth)
- Goblet squats (easier on knees)
- Reverse lunges or split squats
- Leg press with limited range
- Step-ups with low platform

**General Tips:**
- Stop if you feel pain (not just discomfort)
- Focus on controlled movements
- Strengthen muscles around knee (quads, hamstrings)
- Consider swimming or cycling for cardio

**When to See a Doctor:**
- Sharp, sudden pain
- Swelling that doesn't go down
- Knee giving out or locking
- Pain that persists more than a few days

**Training with Lower Back Issues:**

**Exercises to Modify:**
- Deadlifts: Use lighter weight or skip
- Good mornings: Avoid if painful
- Bent-over rows: Try chest-supported instead
- Overhead press: Seated with back support

**Safe Alternatives:**
- Hex bar deadlifts (more upright)
- Romanian deadlifts (lighter, focus on hamstrings)
- Cable rows (chest-supported)
- Leg press instead of squats

**Core Strengthening:**
- Planks (not crunches)
- Dead bugs
- Bird dogs
- McGill big 3

**General Tips:**
- Neutral spine always
- Engage core before every lift
- Don't round back under load
- Stretch hip flexors regularly

**Training with Shoulder Issues:**

**Exercises to Modify:**
- Overhead press: Reduce range or use neutral grip
- Bench press: Use dumbbells, don't go too deep
- Dips: Avoid or use limited range
- Behind-neck press: Never do these

**Safe Alternatives:**
- Landmine press (easier on shoulders)
- Floor press (limits range)
- Incline press (less stress than flat)
- Face pulls (strengthens rear delts)

**Shoulder Health:**
- External rotation exercises
- Band pull-aparts daily
- Stretch pecs and front delts
- Strengthen rotator cuff

**Red Flags:**
- Sharp pain during movement
- Pain that doesn't improve with rest
- Weakness or instability
- Night pain

nutrition_guides.content:
**Nutrition for Fat Loss:**

**Calorie Deficit:**
- Eat 300-500 calories below maintenance
- Don't go too aggressive (no more than 1% bodyweight loss per week)
- Track calories for accuracy

**Protein Priority:**
- 0.8-1g per pound of bodyweight
- Preserves muscle during fat loss
- Most satiating macronutrient
- Examples: chicken, fish, eggs, Greek yogurt, protein powder

**Meal Timing:**
- Eat protein at every meal
- Pre-workout: Carbs for energy (1-2 hours before)
- Post-workout: Protein + carbs for recovery

**Hydration:**
- Drink 0.5-1 oz per pound bodyweight
- More if exercising or hot weather

**Common Mistakes:**
- Cutting calories too low (slows metabolism)
- Not eating enough protein (lose muscle)
- Eliminating entire food groups (unsustainable)
- Not tracking accurately

**Nutrition for Muscle Gain:**

**Calorie Surplus:**
- Eat 200-400 calories above maintenance
- Slow, controlled gain (0.5-1 lb per week)
- Too fast = more fat gain

**Protein:**
- 0.8-1g per pound bodyweight
- Spread throughout day
- Within 2 hours post-workout

**Carbs:**
- Fuel for workouts
- 2-3g per pound bodyweight
- Time around workouts

**Fats:**
- Don't neglect (hormones need fat)
- 0.3-0.5g per pound bodyweight

**Meal Frequency:**
- 3-5 meals per day
- Protein at each meal
- Pre and post-workout nutrition matters most

**Supplements:**
- Creatine (5g daily)
- Protein powder (if needed to hit goals)
- Multi-vitamin (cover bases)
